newsitem.title: USA: Nuclear waste disposal bill offered in U.S. Senate.
newsitem.headline: Nuclear waste disposal bill offered in U.S. Senate.

text.p: Two senators Tuesday introduced a bill to set up a temporary storage dump in the Nevada desert for spent fuel from nuclear power reactors, a measure President Clinton threatened to veto last year.
Senate Energy Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski, an Alaska Republican, called the measure which is being pushed by the nuclear power industry a committee priority.
Murkowski said he planned to raise the issue at an upcoming confirmation hearing for Federico Pena, Clinton's choice to be energy secretary.

"I think the administration may be ready to solve this problem," Murkowski said in a statement. "They know it's irresponsible to keep piling high-level radioactive materials near homes and schools at 80 locations in 41 states," said Murkowski, who co-sponsored the bill with fellow Republican Larry Craig of Idaho.
The Senate passed the bill to build a central storage site last session by 63-37, four votes sort of the margin needed to override the Clinton administration's threatened veto.
The House did not vote on a temporary nuclear waste dump bill last year after the White House's veto threat.
Nevada's congressional delegation opposed the bill which would have put the temporary site near the only long-term storage site under consideration at Nevada's Yucca Mountain.
The Clinton administration opposed it, arguing the temporary dump would divert resources from building a long-term facility and would bypass environmental laws.
